To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) intimacy in a couple is a process of communication and exchange between two people who are in love and who have a common history; (ii) the quality of this communication and exchange depends on the degree of information that each partner can provide to the other, and the way in which they use this information; (iii) the quality of intimacy in a couple can be measured by the degree of information shared by each partner, and by the quality of the information shared by each of them;

intimacy is a process of mutual exchange of information between partners, in which they are required to assess their partner's behavior and to evaluate their own behavior in order to reach a mutual understanding and agreement.

the intimacy levels are: 1) the highest when the partners have the same intimacy level, 2) lower when the partners are in the same intimacy layer, and 3) the lowest when the partners have different intimacy layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can we measure the degree of intimacy of a couple?
the development of a methodological approach to conjugal intimacy based on the theory of information and communication.
the study of the information flow in the couple, and the way this is organized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the conjugal intimacy is a complex system of information exchanges, which are the result of a series of processes, which are in themselves the result of the couple's history and the way they have been educated to live.

the conjugal couple, in the process of intimacy, is a system that is in a state of constant change and evolution, and that the therapist is not a neutral observer but rather a co-creator of the process, in a constant search for a balance that allows for the development of the couple.
the conjugal intimacy is a complex phenomenon that is not limited to sexual intercourse and that it is necessary to take into account the various layers in which it develops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information that is exchanged between the couple, the information that the therapist receives, and the information the couple receives from the therapist, are the three layers of the intimacy.

intimacy is the process of sharing information in the couple, which is the result of a process of selection and transformation of information that is not only cognitive, but also emotional and physical.

intimacy is a complex process of information exchange, which is not only a matter of quantity but also of quality, and which is not only an exchange of information but an exchange of information with a specific purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the therapist is not the only person in charge of evaluating the intimacy of the couple.
intimacy is a process of information exchange, which is not only a technical process, but also a relational and symbolic one.
the therapist is not the only source of knowledge in the process of therapy, but rather that the therapist and the couple together can create new forms of knowledge and meaning in their relationship.
